title: Containers: ECS, EKS, Fargate & App Runner
summary: Run containers with the right orchestrator and launch type, and scale them.
tldr: **ECS** is AWS's own orchestrator and the simplest answer. **EKS** is managed Kubernetes: pick it when the question mentions existing Kubernetes manifests, Helm or portability.
**Fargate** removes the servers: no nodes to patch or scale, each task or pod gets its own isolated compute. **Fargate Spot** cuts cost for interruptible tasks.
Scale in two layers: tasks/pods (**ECS Service Auto Scaling**, Kubernetes HPA) and, on EC2, the nodes (**ECS capacity providers with managed scaling**, Cluster Autoscaler or Karpenter).

keyFacts.text: A capacity provider strategy such as `FARGATE base 2, weight 1` + `FARGATE_SPOT weight 3` keeps 2 tasks on regular capacity and puts ~75% of extra tasks on Spot.
Fargate Spot tasks get a two-minute warning (SIGTERM plus an EventBridge event) before interruption, so only interruption-tolerant tasks belong there.
The **task execution role** lets ECS pull ECR images, send logs and inject Secrets Manager or Parameter Store secrets. The **task role** gives your application code its AWS permissions.
On EKS, a **Fargate profile** selects pods by namespace and labels. Fargate pods can't run DaemonSets, GPUs, privileged containers or EBS volumes.
ECS **service discovery** registers tasks in AWS Cloud Map and a Route 53 private hosted zone, so services find each other by DNS name without a load balancer each.
The ECS **deployment circuit breaker** with rollback stops a failing rolling update and returns to the last working task definition automatically.
App Runner no longer accepts new customers; existing ones can keep using it. AWS points new users to **ECS Express Mode** (Fargate service, ALB and scaling from one image).

traps: Fargate Spot tasks can be interrupted; keep a `base` on regular FARGATE for capacity that must stay up.
Fargate Spot is an ECS feature only; EKS doesn't support Fargate Spot.
ECS Service Auto Scaling adds tasks, not EC2 instances. On the EC2 launch type you also need a capacity provider with managed scaling.
Secret and ECR pull permissions belong on the **task execution role**, not the EC2 container instance role or the image.
Lambda is not a fit for a 2-hour, 8-vCPU job. Run it as a scheduled Fargate task.
EBS volumes are AZ-bound. Stateful EKS pods need a node group per AZ so the autoscaler adds nodes in the right zone.
ECR image layers are stored in S3, so pulling privately needs the **S3 gateway endpoint** as well as the ECR endpoints.
